citation.title: Discrete-Time Population Dynamics of Interacting Self-Oscillators

how_reached: Full four-page scan read page by page via the OUP article-pdf route.
why_this_source: This is the paper UNKNOWNS.md and src/lab/k03.py cite for Daido's asymmetric exponent pair. It does not contain it. That is the finding.
observable: FLUCTUATION. sigma = (<B^2> - C^2)^(1/2), the standard deviation of the order parameter of a purely deterministic system. No external field appears.
frequency_class: REGULAR / deterministic-quantile on a LORENTZIAN g. Delta_j = gamma * tan{(j*pi/N) - (N+1)*pi/(2N)}, algebraically the inverse Lorentzian CDF at the midpoint quantiles (2j-1)/(2N). Zero frequency randomness; the randomness is in initial conditions only.

quotes.quote: The Lorentzian distribution of Δ_j was realized approximately using Δ_j=γ×tan{(jπ/N)−(N+1)π/2N}(1≤j≤N).
quotes.bears_on: Frequency class, from primary text: deterministic-quantile Lorentzian, the same construction lorentzian_frequencies() implements.
The observable is a standard deviation of the order parameter — a fluctuation, and note it is sigma, not sigma-squared.

quotes.quote: On the other hand, as to σ, it is possible to show that for 0<|ε−ε_c|≪1   σ̂≃Q_±|ε−ε_c|^{−1/2} ,   (ε≷ε_c)   (7)   where σ̂=lim_{N→∞}√N σ with Q_+=(ε_cQ)^{1/2}/2 and Q_−=(ε_cQ/2)^{1/2}
quotes.bears_on: THE NEGATIVE RESULT. The only fluctuation-exponent statement in this paper gives the SAME exponent 1/2 on both sides of the transition. Only the amplitudes are asymmetric, by a factor sqrt(2). The pair gamma = 1/4, gamma' = 1 is not here.

quotes.quote: Note that our system is purely deterministic, so that fluctuations of B_n measured by σ are not what is induced by external stochastic perturbations, but are of internal origin.
quotes.bears_on: Daido's own words that sigma is an intrinsic fluctuation, not a driven or field response.

numbers: FLUCTUATION | regular Lorentzian | BOTH sides | Eq. (7): sigma-hat ~ Q_+/- |eps - eps_c|^(-1/2). Exponent 1/2 on sigma, i.e. 1 on chi = sigma^2, symmetric. Amplitude ratio Q_+/Q_- = 1/sqrt(2).
ORDER PARAMETER | p. 1462: C ~ A(eps - eps_c)^(1/2), i.e. beta = 1/2.
caveats: The symbol gamma in this paper is the Lorentzian half-width, not a critical exponent. Grepping for 'gamma = 1/4' finds a width, not an exponent.
The numerics are a discrete-time coupled-circle-map model ('Model LDS'), not the continuous-time Kuramoto ODE.
Daido himself cites this paper only as the numerical antecedent to the 1989 letter, not as the source of the asymmetric exponents.
